problem:
What is the standard deviation of the following data set?

$$
-7,\,3,\,-5,\,-1,\,-5
$$

feedback.problem:
What is the standard deviation of the following data set?

$$
7,\,4,\,11,\,2,\,6
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\,\,\,\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-{(\overset{―}{x})}^{2}}
$$

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=5$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (7+4+11+2+6) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot 30 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot ({7}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{11}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (49+16+121+4+36) \\  & =\frac{226}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{226}{5}-{(6)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{226}{5}-36 \\  & =\frac{226-180}{5} \\  & =\frac{46}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{46}{5}}.
$$
